comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that Arfrp1 and AP-1 are required for Vangl2 TGN export (C2, C22, C25-C28). OpenEval focuses on the siRNA knockdown and colocalization data, while peer reviewers describe the evidence as 'convincing' and 'well controlled.' Peer review encompasses additional claims (C3, C36-C37, C73-C76) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Both support the requirement of AP-1 subunits (μ1-adaptin and β1-adaptin) for Vangl2 trafficking (C3, C36-C37). OpenEval evaluates this as a distinct result based on Figure 5 data, while peer reviewers group it with the broader Arfrp1/AP-1 findings without specific challenge.

Both support the YYXXF motif's functional importance for Vangl2 trafficking (C5, C30-C32, C62, C80). OpenEval emphasizes sequence conservation and mutagenesis data, while peer reviewers accept the motif identification but request mechanistic discussion about why motif mutation causes complete block versus partial block with Arfrp1 knockdown.

Both support the YYXXF motif requirement for μ1-adaptin binding (C6, C33-C35). OpenEval highlights the three independent binding assays providing robust evidence, while peer reviewers accept the data but request discussion of why AP-2/AP-3 don't recognize this signal.

Both support the GTP-dependent interaction between Arfrp1 and AP-1 (C29, C76). OpenEval evaluates the affinity chromatography and mass spectrometry data as supported, while peer reviewers include C76 in their broader acceptance of the Arfrp1-AP-1 pathway without specific challenge.

Both support the reconstitution data showing Arfrp1-GTP recruits AP-1 and that Vangl2 enhances this recruitment (C38-C43). OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive liposome flotation assay data, while peer reviewers find it 'of particular interest' that Arf1 cannot replace Arfrp1, requesting discussion of structural precedent and amino acid conservation.

Both address Frizzled-6 independence from Arfrp1/AP-1 (C4, C48-C50, C55), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED based on siRNA knockdown and temperature shift data, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, noting the conclusion is 'not too surprising' and requesting the authors 'tone down the statement' and provide additional temperature shift/cycloheximide experiments similar to PTK7.

Both address PTK7 dependence on Arfrp1 (C53-C54), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED based on sequence alignment and temperature shift experiments, while peer reviewers express UNCERTAINTY, questioning why 'such a different experimental strategy was required' and requesting the authors 'tone down the statement that PTK7 depends on Arfrp1.'

Both support the finding that kinase-dead PKD blocks TGN export of both Vangl2 and Frizzled-6 (C57-C59). OpenEval explicitly rates this as SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it without challenge or comment.

Both support Vangl2's preferential binding to Arfrp1 over Arf1 (C44-C46). OpenEval emphasizes the GST pull-down data and YYXXF-dependence supporting indirect interaction through AP-1, while peer reviewers accept the finding and request discussion of how differential binding allows cooperativity.

Both support the negative result that Arl1 knockdown does not affect Vangl2 (C73-C74). OpenEval evaluates this as helping define Arfrp1 specificity, while peer reviewers include it in their broader acceptance of the Arfrp1-AP-1 pathway and request discussion of Arl1/Golgin245 roles.

Both rate the mechanistic model about distinct AP-1 conformations and alternative binding sites (C7, C63, C95-C97) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the model is plausible but lacks direct structural evidence (acknowledged in C103), while peer reviewers request enhanced discussion including structural precedent and amino acid conservation between Arfrp1 and Arf1.

Both support the negative controls demonstrating specificity (C23, C75). OpenEval emphasizes that other Golgi Arfs don't affect Vangl2 and that AP-2/AP-3 don't bind Arfrp1-GTP, while peer reviewers include these in their broader acceptance of the well-controlled experiments.

Both address differential binding of PCP proteins to Arfrp1/μ1-adaptin (C51). OpenEval rates this as SUPPORTED based on GST pull-down data showing only Vangl2 binds, while peer reviewers include this in their broader uncertainty about differential trafficking claims, requesting additional experiments.

Both rate speculative proposals about mechanisms and biological significance (C101-C102, C104-C105) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes these claims lack direct experimental support and the alternative binding site hypothesis has no structural evidence, while peer reviewers request discussion of structural precedent and alternative binding sites similar to APP/AP-4.
